title: To suppose the Saints see all men and hear all thoughts is to give them something divine
source_text: XXXIV. Quod si quis supponat Sanctos in caelo cum Christo regnantes, posse simul omnes homines, in quacunque mundi parte positos, intueri, eorumque preces audire, & cogitationes nosse, atque etiam opem quam ab ipsis postulant ferre, & quaecunque fiunt in eorum honorem percipere atque agnoscere: hoc ipso putant Sanctis divinum quid tribui, & ea de quibus jam agimus honoris signa, non amplius ad humanum, sed ad divinum cultum pertinere.
pass_a_gloss: But if someone supposes that the Saints reigning in heaven with Christ can at once behold all men, set in whatever part of the world, and hear their prayers, and know their thoughts, and also bring the help they ask of them, and perceive and recognize whatever is done in their honor: by this very thing they think something divine is attributed to the Saints, and the signs of honor of which we now speak no longer belong to human cult, but to divine cult.
pass_b_english: If the Saints in glory are supposed to see everyone everywhere at once, hear their prayers, know their thoughts, give the help asked, and notice everything done in their honor, something divine has been given them.
The signs of honor in question then cease to be human cult and become divine cult.

choices.why: Knowledge of hearts is the divine mark that reclassifies the cult.
rejected: knowing what is told them by a letter
